reasons: The desk scale value appears unused.
The toast handler does nothing, so messages are dropped.
Popups such as the command palette are drawn only in classic mode.
No test is visible for this large page.

terms.meaning: A shared place where the app keeps data and state that many screens can read and change.
The small state library used for the stores.
A React tool that runs a piece of code at a set moment, such as on load or when a value changes.
A repeating timer that moves something forward, here once per second.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports
sections.what: Pulls in the state stores, the login screen, the layouts, every room and screen, and the popups.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: Home (part 1)
sections.title: Local page state and desk scaling
sections.what: Holds the page's own choices: which layout shows, whether the cat intro is done, and which desk room is open. Also calculates a scale factor so the desk fits the window.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps view choices on the page rather than in the shared store.
sections.watch_out: The scale factor is calculated and updated, but the visible code never uses it, so it may have no effect.

sections.name: Home (part 2)
sections.title: Mode switch events and startup
sections.what: Listens for window events that switch between desk and classic mode or replay the cat intro. On startup it checks sign-in, loads saved data, checks the streak, and copies the user's name and role into the profile.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets any component change mode without passing props down.
sections.watch_out: If the startup functions change identity, the loading runs again.

sections.name: Home: if
sections.title: Focus timer, shortcuts and first screens
sections.what: Ticks the focus timer every second while it runs, handles the keyboard shortcuts, shows the login screen when no one is signed in, and starts the desk with the cat intro.
sections.why: Likely reason: these global behaviours must run on every screen.
sections.watch_out: Shortcuts are ignored only in plain input and text area fields, so typing in other editable areas could trigger them.

sections.name: Home: if
sections.title: Desk home and room header
sections.what: Shows the desk home base after the intro. For any other room it shows a header with a back button, the user's level and XP, and the AI button.
sections.why: Likely reason: a consistent header for each room.
sections.watch_out: The room title is the room id in capitals, so a new room with a poor id shows raw text.

sections.name: Home (part 5)
sections.title: Room content and header buttons
sections.what: Shows the open room's content and lets the user open the AI assistant, switch to classic mode, or go back home.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The toast handler is empty, so any message sent to it is silently dropped.

sections.name: Home (part 6)
sections.title: Bottom room tray
sections.what: Shows eleven icon buttons along the bottom for moving between rooms, with the current room highlighted, and includes the AI drawer.
sections.why: Likely reason: quick navigation in desk mode.
sections.watch_out: The room list is typed in here by hand, so a new room must be added here and also handled where rooms are drawn.

sections.name: Home (part 7)
sections.title: Classic layout and global popups
sections.what: Shows the classic sidebar, header and selected screen, and mounts the global popups and the floating add button.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the older full layout available for users who prefer it.
sections.watch_out: Popups such as the command palette are drawn only in classic mode, so in desk mode the shortcut keys change state without showing anything.

summary: The home page that decides what the user sees: the login screen, the cat intro, the desk room layout, or the classic sidebar layout.
purpose: Acts as the main switchboard of the app, choosing which screen or room to show and handling global keyboard shortcuts.
why: Likely reason: one page controls the two layout modes so they can share startup logic.
how: 1) Reads login, data and view state from the stores. 2) Starts sign-in checks, saved data loading and the focus timer ticker. 3) Listens for keyboard shortcuts. 4) Shows the login screen if no one is signed in. 5) Shows the desk layout with its intro, home base and rooms, or the classic sidebar layout.
inputs: Login state, saved data, focus timer state, keyboard input, and window events from other components.
outputs: The full screen the user sees, plus changes to stored settings and timer state.
risks: Several flags are only handled in one layout. The desk scale value is calculated but not used in the visible code. The toast handler is empty.
debug: If the wrong screen shows, check the isAuthenticated check and the uiMode and activeDeskRoom values. If shortcuts do nothing in desk mode, check whether the matching modal is rendered only in classic mode. If the focus timer stops, check the ticker effect.
